designSummary: Cross-classification of index test and reference standard in randomly sampled messages from clinics A and B after clinic C paused.
sampleSize: With clinic C paused, clinics A and B supply about 140 sampled messages per week, so reaching about 95 urgent messages at 4 percent takes about 17 weeks instead of 12, still within the study period. Few messages in languages other than English come from clinics A and B, so sensitivity for them cannot be estimated with a useful interval; it is reported as a limitation, with a plan to add clinic C when it resumes.
primaryAnalysis: Sensitivity and specificity with Wilson intervals, overall and by clinic, from the two-by-two table against the adjudicated reference standard.
secondaryAnalysis: Sensitivity for patients over 75 and, descriptively, for messages in languages other than English; kappa before adjudication; description of every false negative.
missingData: Messages the flag failed to score are counted and reported; they are treated as not flagged in a sensitivity analysis.
multiplicity: One primary measure; subgroups are descriptive with intervals.
overfittingGuards: No threshold tuning of the flag
summary: About 17 weeks at 140 messages per week for 95 urgent messages; the language subgroup can no longer be estimated precisely.
